2609.23508.title: Heating in human-HVAC interaction for smart homes: An interdisciplinary overview
2609.23508.paper_summary: As part of HVAC systems, residential heating provides foundational infrastructure for human habitation in cold weather. However, research on how residents interact with HVAC systems, particularly heating systems, remains fragmented across architecture, engineering, informatics, physiology, psychology, sociology, and design. Based on 541 studies from these fields, this review integrates interdisciplinary research on Heating in Human-HVAC Interaction in smart homes.The resulting synthesis is conceptualized through the Situated Interaction Dynamics of control and feedback between users and systems. User-initiated interactions involve monitoring past and present system performance and planning future operation, while system-initiated interactions rely on sensor networks to trigger automation or provide information enabling user action. These interaction dynamics connect Residents' Experience and Practices with Heating in HVAC System Mechanics. Residents' Experience and Practices include thermal comfort and energy management, where thermal comfort involves both individual physiological and psychological experiences of indoor climate and social practices shaped by norms, empathy, and negotiation among cohabitants. Heating in HVAC System Mechanics includes thermal conditions and energy performance. Thermal conditions concern the regulation of air temperature, mean radiant temperature, air velocity, and relative humidity, while energy performance concerns efficiency and environmental impact. This overview highlights four interdisciplinary tensions: sensed versus lived conditions, personalization versus negotiation, efficiency versus health, and automation versus agency. The resulting framework offers a conceptual lens to interpret heating interactions and design Human-HVAC Interaction that balances IEQ-driven healthy thermal conditions, affordability, and sustainability.
2609.23508.paper_summary_zh: 作為HVAC系統的一部分，住宅供暖為寒冷天氣中的人類居住提供了基礎設施。然而，關於居民如何與HVAC系統，特別是供暖系統互動的研究，仍然在建築、工程、資訊學、生理學、心理學、社會學和設計等領域中支離破碎。基於來自這些領域的541項研究，本綜述整合了智能家居中人類-HVAC互動中的供暖的跨學科研究。所得到的綜合通過用戶與系統之間的控制和反饋的情境互動動態進行概念化。用戶主動的互動涉及監控過去和現在的系統性能以及規劃未來的運行，而系統主動的互動則依賴於傳感器網絡來觸發自動化或提供使用戶行動的資訊。這些互動動態將居民的體驗和實踐與HVAC系統機械中的供暖聯繫起來。居民的體驗和實踐包括熱舒適和能源管理，其中熱舒適涉及個體生理和心理的室內氣候體驗，以及由規範、同理心和同居者之間的協商所塑造的社會實踐。HVAC系統機械中的供暖包括熱條件和能源性能。熱條件關注空氣溫度、平均輻射溫度、空氣速度和相對濕度的調節，而能源性能則關注效率和環境影響。本概述突出了四個跨學科的緊張關係：感知的條件與生活的條件、個性化與協商、效率與健康，以及自動化與主體性。所得到的框架提供了一個概念視角，以解釋供暖互動並設計平衡IEQ驅動的健康熱條件、可負擔性和可持續性的人類-HVAC互動。
